Vincent Souly is among about 1,130 African priests who oversee Italian churches — approximately 4% of Italy’s clergy, not including more junior church positions.

Father Souly has served as a Roman Catholic priest for 15 years in the province of Prato and built warm relationships with his predominantly Italian flocks and is embraced by many parishioners. He is part of a historic wave of immigration that is changing Europe. Italy, with 12% born overseas, has one of the largest immigrant populations on the continent — a remarkable reversal for a nation that once helped to fuel mass emigration to America.

The priest’s life highlights a nuance of that changing Italy. {"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787757773,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787757773,"created_at_utc":1787757773,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3972311127367788789,"pk":"18114696653072413","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"18114696653072413","text":"In the past two years, #JackOConnell has played a vampire in “Sinners” and a cult leader in the “28 Years Later” films. But to take on the role of tabloid editor Larry Lamb, he got even more comfortable with suave, alluring menace.

“His prerogative is very simple,” O’Connell says over Zoom from London. “He’s fixated on sales numbers and whatever it’s going to take to keep that figure rising. He’ll stop at nothing — and that means bending the rules. It was very naughty.”

Netflix’s “Ink,” directed by Danny Boyle and set to open the Venice Film Festival on Sept. 2, is as naughty as its central character. Lamb was the real-life editor of The Sun who — hired in 1969 by press baron Rupert Murdoch to help the tabloid break into the U.K. newspaper industry — pioneered such practices as publishing nude pictures of “Page 3 Girls.” The provocative biopic, however, is not intended as a hit piece.

“One of the dangers with doing anything about Rupert Murdoch is that everybody monster-izes him,” says director Danny Boyle, “as though he’s forced everybody to read The Sun! We are all responsible for this.”

Read the full cover story at the link in bio.

#RupertGrint has joined the cast of “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child” on Broadway, where he’ll play an adult version of his iconic role Ron Weasley.

The #HarryPotter actor will appear on Broadway from Feb. 2 to May 30, 2027.

“Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old and I can’t wait to meet him again in this stage of life,” Grint said in a statement. “There is something so full-circle and so special about stepping back into Ron’s shoes now when we are both fathers; it is somehow both very familiar and completely new. And the joy of being back on Broadway, this time in a role that defined so much of my life is truly exciting.”

Grint’s casting comes after the success of #TomFelton’s run in the play as an elder Draco Malfoy, which has just been extended through Jan. 3 and resulted in a hefty box office increase.

Even the whizziest strategies can underperform for career-wreckingly long periods.

The momentum trade—of buying recent winners—has minted fortunes. If the past few weeks are anything to go by, that might be faltering. 

Great investors must be able to cut their losses without avoiding risk in the first place. These qualities do not usually co-exist in the same person. When they do, that person is likely to be unusual.

Great money managers are rare. Tap the link in our bio to read why they require a big dose of luck, and a distinctly odd character.

In a dramatic capitulation, the owner of Facebook and Instagram agreed to the financial penalties for violating federal child privacy and states’ consumer protection laws, the states announced. Meta also agreed to limit how long teenagers can spend on its platforms and to bans on features that stoke mental health issues.

The settlement amount is one of the highest ever paid by a tech company to states.

⁣
For the country’s largest businesses, staying nimble can be a challenge. Decades of established systems and enormous workforces can make it harder to continually adapt, test and push an industry forward.⁣
⁣
Forbes’ inaugural list of America’s Most Innovative Large Companies looks at which corporate giants are doing just that. {"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787819489,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787819489,"created_at_utc":1787819489,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3972399614481543424,"pk":"18135811507620849","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"18135811507620849","text":"Over the last 18 months, the noise has grown around a new type of subculture, one rooted in onanism, self-pleasure—whatever you want to call it—and the people who are doing it for hours and hours on end in pursuit of a near-mythical zen-like state of bliss. These are the gooners, the internet’s slick-palmed folk devils, and they have been getting louder and prouder about their strange antics as the media’s fascination with them has boomed.

But is gooning a bona fide sub cultural community, with its own lore, slang, and social codes? Or just an internet joke that got out of hand? Making her VICE debut, host Noelle Perdue heads to AVN—the world’s largest adult expo—for its first event since gooning exploded into the mainstream, to meet gooners, to listen to their fantasies and anxieties, and to get to the bottom of what gooning really is.

“The Wild Goon Chase” premieres today at VICE: Members Only, watch it in full now through the links in our bio.

{"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787710722,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787710722,"created_at_utc":1787710722,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3971922607377970502,"pk":"17915676033438799","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"17915676033438799","text":"Dolly Parton, the beloved country-music superstar known for writing about the lives of working-class people in more than 3,000 recorded songs and, in later years, for giving away nearly 300 million books to children around the world, died in Nashville. She was 80. 

Her larger-than-life hair, excess in rhinestones, surgical implants, and cosmetic work concealed the iron will through which she confronted the day’s realities with her craft. She wrote and sang with a woman’s voice and heart about topics that touched her gender, like stories of stillborn births (“Down From Dover”), suicide (“The Bridge”), shame (“Just Because I’m a Woman”), sexual assault (“A Gamble Either Way”), isolation (“Two Doors Down”), and prostitution (“The Bargain Store”).

Parton was a genius from humble origins. Because of them, she remained vulnerable, even relatable, in the public eye. Her cycle of resurrections, the highs and lows, didn’t seem to change her much over the years, even as the highs garnered her over half a billion dollars. Hers was a Cinderella story.

Read more about Dolly Parton’s life, written by @shimaoliaee, at the link in bio.

{"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787765735,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787765735,"created_at_utc":1787765735,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3972389292022302772,"pk":"18077770163508260","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"18077770163508260","text":"Tim Curry, the English actor who became a massively popular cult figure thanks to his performances in "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," "Clue" and the TV miniseries "It," has died. He was 80.

A classic character actor, Curry often portrayed supercillious Brits, crafty villains (he played the devil more than once) and befuddled sidekicks.

He demanded attention as soon as he walked on screen as Frank-N-Furter in 1975’s "Rocky Horror," boldly strolling past rows of acolytes and ripping off a robe to reveal a corset and stockings. His Lord of Darkness, from 1985’s fantasy film "Legend," was equipped with giant horns and a tomato-red face, but it was Curry's casual delivery, dripping with menace, that elevated the role to more than a caricature.

Curry had a working actor's distance — and an Englishman's understatement — toward the parts he played. Describing Pennywise, the demonic clown he played in 1990’s "It," perhaps Stephen King's most frightening creation, he told the magazine Fangoria, "Basically, he's completely irredeemable; he's the kind of chap that's entirely without charm."

As for Frank-N-Furter, Curry was equally detached, remembering the beloved role with "bemused tolerance." He told NPR's "Fresh Air" in 2005 that the charismatic role was a challenge to overcome.

"(It) was so out there, so kind of outrageous, that I was a very quiet boy for a while, just to make sure that people got it — that that wasn't necessarily who I was," he said.

Tap the link in our bio to read more about Curry's life.

Security forces led by the Nepali Army said that 114 people had been airlifted to safety. According to a report from Reuters, the company could pay up to $16.68 billion. The settlement allows CEO Mark Zuckerberg and the company to avoid a high-stakes trial, whose consequences could have remade how the tech industry operates. The proposed agreement will need to be approved by the court, but it brings 52 US attorneys general into the deal, not just those who were party to the original lawsuit.⁠
⁠

⁠
Parton remains one of the most prolific songwriters who ever lived. By her estimation, she wrote more than 3,000 songs—more than 1,000 of which were recorded and released.⁠
⁠
Her entertainment empire, worth more than $500 million, spanned multiple venues including the Dollywood theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tenn., which draws more than two million visitors annually.⁠
⁠
The multiplatinum recording artist and Hollywood actress was also a philanthropist. To honor her father, Robert Lee Parton, who never learned to read and write, she started the Imagination Library, which donated more than 200 million books to children around the world. In 2020, she contributed $1 million to Vanderbilt University for virus research, which helped kickstart Moderna’s Covid-19 vaccine.⁠
⁠
Read more at the link in our bio.⁠

⁠

“In previous interviews or conversations I’ve had around my other albums, I know I have said exactly that, like, ‘Now I’m here, and I’ve arrived!’” But it wasn’t true then, Abrams tells Rolling Stone, not really. And it isn’t true now. “The theme to me is trying to paint an accurate picture of all of these different versions of who you are in this decade when you are sort of one foot in a past life and one foot in the future.”

{"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787742265,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787742265,"created_at_utc":1787742265,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3972192413248985061,"pk":"18065792651501761","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"18065792651501761","text":"Over the course of the past year, OpenAI has faced a series of challenges: key leadership and research departures, rogue AI agents attacking other companies, lawsuits from Apple and Elon Musk, and increased competition in the AI race from its rival, Anthropic.

“We clearly had some missteps as a company,” says OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. “Both in terms of product direction and specifically on pretraining in research, we fell behind where we wanted to be.”

The company, which is preparing for an upcoming IPO, remains in an enviable position. ChatGPT is one of the most popular AI products in the world, though it is no longer the cornerstone of the company’s future. OpenAI has refocused its priorities, investing heavily into computing and winding down multiple projects including the video-generation app Sora. Altman concedes the company had spread itself too thin.

Even amid growing backlash against AI progress, OpenAI is positioning itself to be among the world’s most consequential companies for years to come. As co-founder and president Greg Brockman puts it, “We are looking at transforming the entire economy.”

TIME got unparalleled access inside OpenAI in August, spending dozens of hours talking to more than 20 of its leaders, employees, investors, and customers. Read more from our interviews at the link in bio.

Not even a quarter of the way into an expected 19-day federal trial over Meta’s alleged failure to protect young users, the social media giant agreed to settle the case. The company has agreed to pay up to $16.7 billion to 51 US states and territories, and make substantive product changes for how teens engage with its platforms.

Attorneys general representing some of the 29 US states that had taken Meta to trial announced the deal on Wednesday, shortly before Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri was set to return to the witness stand. In a separate announcement detailing the settlement, Meta urged YouTube and TikTok to adopt similar changes to their platforms.

The settlement is a stunning development; while other social media services including YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok resolved similar lawsuits out of court, Meta has repeatedly chosen to go to trial. Earlier this year, it lost state trials in California and New Mexico, notching nearly $1 billion in penalties. The company’s first federal trial on the youth issues began last week and threatened to leave the company on the hook for what it estimated to be over $1 trillion in damages.

Severe flooding was reported across the regions of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Gorkha, north of the Nepalese capital Kathmandu. The majority of the flooding has occurred along the Trishuli and Bhotekoshi rivers in the north of the country.

Nepal’s Tourism Board said that 384 people were missing as a result of the flooding, including 291 foreign nationals and 91 Nepali citizens. Read more at the link in bio.

{"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1783263278,"created_at_for_fb_app":1783263278,"created_at_utc":1783263278,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3933173798887853161,"pk":"17953203468189634","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"17953203468189634","text":"Presenting the summer 2026 edition of VICE magazine: The Self-Destruction Issue, 132 scintillating pages of lizard-brain chicanery inspired by a species that is constantly finding groundbreaking new ways to destroy itself.

We investigate a diabolical Miami cult, hang out with the Yakuza, chronicle the face-destroying antics of devout Taoists in Phuket, expose a barely-believable and growing armed response to a sex-pest problem within the Pokémon cosplay community, and shine a light on inventive new anti-conscription measures in Ukraine.

The issue stars such luminaries as Antoine D’Agata, Will Self, Bertie Brandes, Sean Thor Conroe, Elias Rønnenfelt, Opioid Crisis Lookbook, Simon Reynolds, Mattha Busby, Julie Poly, Nick Dove, Noelle Perdue, Giancarlo DiTrapano, and our new columnists Biz Sherbert, Caia Hagel, and Emma Garland.

Oh, and Chris Nieratko returns with his fabled SKINEMA column.

You can pre-order the issue now through the links in our bio. Better yet, why not subscribe? That way, you never miss an issue.

“Self-destruction has killed some of my best friends. It has also given me the greatest moments of my life and could’ve been the theme of every issue of VICE since its inception. Sometimes you just have to let bygones be bygones and give a set of catastrophically harmful behavioral patterns their dues.”
KEVIN LEE KHARAS
Editor In Chief

“I have channeled many decades of malignant energy caused by poor decision-making into this one unique publication. I hope that you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed ruining everything good that ever happened to me.”
BEN DITTO
Global Editorial Director

But media outlets can’t serve that role if they’re bankrupt. And as a result, news readers often find themselves blocked by paywalls from reading important stories about government business.

"That experience is particularly frustrating for readers who are unable to access the groundbreaking investigative reports outlets like Wired magazine have been publishing, particularly over the first couple months of the Trump administration," the Freedom of the Press Foundation release reads. "Fortunately, Wired has a solution — it’s going to stop paywalling articles that are primarily based on public records obtained through the Freedom of Information Act."

Access to journalism based on public records is more important than ever at this moment, with government websites and records disappearing, DOGE doing its best to operate outside the public’s view, and the National Archive in disarray.

We’re excited to be the first publication to partner with @freedomofthepressfoundation to offer this for our new coverage. {"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787759139,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787759139,"created_at_utc":1787759139,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3972333482113750502,"pk":"18335543467262247","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"18335543467262247","text":"Tim Curry, the offbeat British actor who specialized in playing eccentrics like the seductive, cross-dressing scientist Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show and such fiendish villains as Pennywise the Clown from Stephen King’s It, has died. He was 80.

Curry died Tuesday night at his home in Los Angeles, TMZ reported. He suffered a major stroke in 2012.

Curry joined Rocky Horror in the original stage production at a tiny upstairs venue at London’s Royal Court Theatre, stuck with the sexual farce as it moved to larger London venues and Broadway and then starred with a young Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick in the 1975 Fox movie adaptation. 

At the movies, audience members would dress up as their favorite characters, bring props and throw items around the theater as they sang along to favorites like “Time Warp,” “Touch-a-Touch-a-Touch-a-Touch Me” and, performed by Curry, the sensationally bawdy “Sweet Transvestite.”

“It’s a chance for people to try on a few roles for size, maybe help them figure out their own sexuality,” Curry said of the film in a 2005 interview with NPR. “I’ve certainly had some very interesting and moving mail from people who’ve said, ‘Thanks for helping me figure out who I was,’ and that’s very nice.”

{"can_view_more_preview_comments":false,"caption":{"bit_flags":0,"content_type":"comment","created_at":1787698827,"created_at_for_fb_app":1787698827,"created_at_utc":1787698827,"did_report_as_spam":false,"is_covered":false,"is_created_by_media_owner":true,"is_ranked_comment":true,"media_id":3971828054654492217,"pk":"17954253558227750","private_reply_status":0,"share_enabled":true,"status":"Active","strong_id__":"17954253558227750","text":"The NBA had “Magic” and “The Answer.” The WNBA now has “The Spectacle.”⁠
⁠
Her name is Olivia Miles and, in a pair of heavy, bulbous, delightfully old-school glasses, the Minnesota Lynx guard has emerged from the WNBA’s summer of chaos to become the league’s best rookie in years.⁠
⁠
With a mix of prolific scoring, laser-targeted passing and inventive ball handling, Miles has all but locked down the league’s Rookie of the Year award. But her role in propelling the Lynx to the league’s best record with a few weeks left of the regular season has also put her on the shortlist for MVP. If Miles wins it, she’ll join Candace Parker as the only player to win both awards in the same year.⁠
⁠
“I knew I belonged, and I knew I was going to do well,” Miles said earlier this season. “But I didn’t think I was going to do this well.”⁠
⁠
Miles, who starred at Notre Dame before playing a season at TCU, was drafted by the Lynx second overall behind former UConn star Azzi Fudd—a choice that already looks like a steal. Miles ranks among the league’s top 10 in points per game and assists, and her 3-point percentage is among the best in the league for a starting guard.⁠
⁠
Muffet McGraw, the two-time NCAA championship coach at Notre Dame who recruited Miles but retired before she played her first game, had no hesitation in picking out Miles’ greatest asset. Her guard in glasses, she said, had uncanny vision on the court.⁠
⁠
“She has a strong belief in herself and she can put things behind her,” McGraw said. “Turn it over? Move on. She doesn’t dwell on things. And I just think she really wants to be great.”⁠
⁠

Curry appeared in numerous movies, often as a hammy villain, was nominated three times for a Tony Award for Broadway roles and performed voice work in many animated films and TV shows.
 
But among his best-known roles was Dr. Frank N. Furter, which came in his debut film, the outrageous, crowd-pleasing horror-comedy-musical "The Rocky Horror Picture Show."

The country megastar had a glittering career, with 25 number-one hits on Billboard’s Hot Country chart and 11 Grammy Awards. 

She could sound weary and bemused, as in “9 to 5”, in which she pours herself “a cup of ambition” before battling rush-hour traffic; or sharp and piercing, as in “Jolene”, in which she begs another woman not to “take my man”.

A fuming, friendless Mr Trump, so weakened by his own blunders and by plunging approval ratings that he retreats to the gilded fastness of his White House, there to tinker with plans for his ballroom and memorial arch? That is a vision that many governments would cheer.

But the American president sees himself as an alpha male to his core. Now that his dominance is threatened, the world will find him more disruptive than ever.

Instead of dreaming of lame ducks, foreign governments should study mountain gorillas—and the violence of which an ageing silverback male is capable, when it senses its time is up.

Tap the link in our bio to learn why anyone hoping to see Mr Trump chastened by failure is misjudging the man.

“A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right. But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one. “She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist.”

“Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the
